title: AI Meeting Transcription Tools Compared: Fireflies vs Otter.ai vs TL;DV
description: 3 meetings a day and can't keep up with notes? Real-world testing of 4 AI meeting transcription tools — Fireflies.ai, Otter.ai, TL;DV, and Granola — on transcription accuracy, summary quality, and value for solopreneurs.
content:
## Why You Need an AI Meeting Transcription Tool

If you're a founder, freelancer, or team lead who sits through 3+ meetings a day, you know the pain: by the time the call ends, you've forgotten half of what was decided. You scramble to piece together notes from scattered scribbles, Slack messages, and vague memory. This is exactly the problem AI meeting transcription tools solve — and they've gotten remarkably good at it over the past year.

I've spent the last several months putting the leading tools through real-world testing across client calls, team standups, product reviews, and brainstorming sessions. Here's what I found.

## Fireflies.ai

**Transcription Accuracy: 95%+ (English)**

Fireflies is the current market leader for good reason. It integrates directly with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Slack — once connected, it automatically joins your meetings, records everything, and delivers a full transcript and AI summary to your inbox within minutes of the call ending. You don't have to think about it; it just works.

The speaker identification is excellent. Fireflies builds a voice profile for each participant and accurately attributes dialogue across multi-person calls. In a 6-person product review I ran, it correctly identified every speaker, including our new hire who'd only been on two previous calls.

**Summary Quality: ★★★★★**

This is where Fireflies truly shines. Its AI doesn't just dump a wall of text — it structures the summary by topic, with each section containing the discussion points, conclusions, and action items. It can identify "decision moments" and "commitments" in conversations, which is incredibly valuable for project management. The search function across all past meetings is also top-notch; you can find any topic, keyword, or action item in seconds.

**Price: Free tier (limited), Paid from $18/month**

The free tier gives you a limited number of transcription credits. The Pro plan at $18/month per seat is reasonable for what you get. There's also an AI-powered search feature that indexes all your meeting knowledge — that alone is worth the price for teams with lots of calls.

**Drawbacks:** Chinese support is poor (~60% accuracy). No mobile recording app — it depends entirely on calendar integration. Can occasionally miss meetings if the calendar sync hiccups.

## Otter.ai

**Transcription Accuracy: 93%+ (English)**

Otter was one of the early pioneers in this space, and it shows in the polish of the product. The real-time transcription experience is the best of the bunch — as the meeting happens, you see words appear on screen in real time. You can highlight, comment, and add emoji reactions right on the live transcript, which is great for taking non-disruptive notes during a call.

Otter's speaker identification is similarly strong, and it has a clever "voiceprint" system that recognizes repeat participants across multiple meetings. The mobile app is excellent too — you can record in-person meetings or use it as a dictation tool.

**Summary Quality: ★★★★☆**

Otter generates a "Meeting Brief" — a structured summary with an overview, key topics, and action items. It's well-organized but slightly less sophisticated than Fireflies in terms of topic breakdown. Where Otter excels is searchability: you can search for any word spoken across all your meetings and jump directly to that moment in the transcript.

**Price: Free tier (300 min/month), Paid from $16.99/month**

The free tier is generous enough for light users. The Pro plan at $16.99/month adds more transcription hours and advanced features.

**Drawbacks:** No Chinese support at all. Requires a browser extension for automatic meeting joining, which is less seamless than Fireflies' direct integration. The AI summaries can sometimes miss nuanced context.

## TL;DV

**Transcription Accuracy: 92%+ (English)**

TL;DV (Too Long; Didn't View) takes a different approach — it's built around video + synchronized text. Every meeting recording has a full transcript that's time-coded to the video, so clicking any line of text jumps you to that exact moment in the recording. This makes it incredibly easy to revisit specific parts of a conversation without scrubbing through an hour of video.

**Summary Quality: ★★★★☆**

TL;DV's AI is especially good at extracting "highlight reels" — short clips of the most important moments in a meeting. It automatically identifies key decisions, interesting questions, and important announcements, and presents them as shareable clips. This is fantastic for asynchronous communication: instead of forwarding a full recording, you can send a 30-second clip of the relevant part.

The AI also generates concise chapter summaries that let you skim a meeting's structure at a glance. The topic detection is solid, though not as granular as Fireflies.

**Price: Free tier (limited), Paid from $24/month**

The free tier covers about 10 meetings. The paid plan at $24/month is on the pricier side, but the clip-sharing and highlight features are unique value-adds.

**Drawbacks:** Chinese support is basic at best (~70% accuracy). The price-to-feature ratio is less competitive than Fireflies for teams that don't need video clips. No automatic calendar joining — you need to invite the bot manually.

## Granola

**Transcription Accuracy: 90%+ (English)**

Granola is a newer entrant with an interesting twist: it's a local-first desktop app (Mac only currently) that records your system audio and microphone simultaneously. Unlike cloud-based tools, Granola doesn't need to be invited to meetings — it just listens to whatever is playing on your computer. This means it works with any meeting platform, including less common ones like Whereby, BlueJeans, or Webex.

**Summary Quality: ★★★★☆**

Granola's AI summary format is clean and minimal. It structures the output as a timeline of discussion topics with timestamps, making it easy to navigate. The "AI notes" feature is surprisingly good at capturing the essence of a conversation without the fluff. It also offers a "notebook" view where you can manually annotate and add your own notes alongside the AI-generated ones.

**Price: Free in beta, paid TBD**

Granola is currently free while in beta. The team hasn't announced pricing yet, which makes it a great option to try right now.

**Drawbacks:** Mac-only (no Windows or web app). No cloud storage of recordings — everything is local, which means no cross-device access. Still in beta, so features and reliability can vary.

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Feature | Fireflies.ai | Otter.ai | TL;DV | Granola |
|---------|-------------|---------|-------|---------|
| English Accuracy | 95%+ | 93%+ | 92%+ | 90%+ |
| Chinese Support | Poor | None | Basic | None |
| Auto Join Calendar | ✅ Yes | ⚠️ Extension | ❌ Manual | ✅ System audio |
| Real-time Transcript | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Speaker ID | Excellent | Excellent | Good | Good |
| Video Sync | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (best) | ❌ |
| Clip Sharing | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Mobile App | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Starting Price | $18/mo | $16.99/mo | $24/mo | Free (beta) |

## Final Recommendations

**For English-first teams who want maximum automation:** Go with **Fireflies.ai**. It has the best English accuracy, the most seamless auto-join experience, and the most sophisticated AI summaries. The knowledge search across all meetings is a game-changer for teams.

**For real-time collaboration during calls:** **Otter.ai** is your best bet. The live transcript with inline annotations is unmatched. The mobile app also makes it the most flexible for recording in-person meetings.

**For teams that share meeting clips externally:** **TL;DV** is worth the premium. The highlight reel and clip-sharing features are genuinely unique and save tons of time when communicating asynchronously with clients or stakeholders.

**For solo users who want privacy and zero setup:** **Granola** is a fantastic free option during beta. The local-first approach means your recordings stay on your machine, and it works with literally any meeting platform.

**For Chinese-language teams:** None of these English-focused tools handle Chinese well. You'll want to look at Chinese-native solutions like 通义听悟 (Alibaba Cloud's Tingwu) or dedicated CN-market tools.

## Practical Tips

Whichever tool you choose, don't rely on AI summaries blindly. The AI can miss subtle context, sarcasm, or non-verbal cues. My workflow: let the AI generate the first pass of notes and action items, then do a quick 3-minute review to add nuance. This cuts my note-taking time by 80% while preserving the human judgment that AI still can't replicate.

The best meeting transcription tool isn't the one with the most features — it's the one you'll actually use consistently. Start with whichever tool integrates most naturally into your existing workflow, and upgrade from there.
